title: Cost Architect Runway — Initiative dossier for adaptive batching, KV-prefetch and quant profiles
creator: Avery Chen
description: High-level dossier for the Cost Architect Runway initiative: reduce per-token unit cost while preserving SLA and output quality by coordinating three levers — adaptive batching, KV-prefetch (prefix/TTL lifecycle), and guided quantization profiles. This initiative coordinates PM, Eng, Design and Research to produce an experiment matrix, rollout gating criteria, adoption playbook, and OKR targets for H1. Workstreams include: 1) runtime integration and metrics plumbing; 2) experiment harness and A/B; 3) console UX for cost/reliability knobs; 4) customer communication and migration playbook. Deliverables: experiment registry, two production rollouts (canary then phased), cost SLO dashboard, and adoption guide for customers and account teams.
acceptance_criteria: Produce experiment matrix with 30 hypotheses across workloads (chat, generation, embeddings)
Demonstrate >=15% median unit-cost reduction on 3 representative customer workloads without >5% quality regression per eval set
Console exposes per-route suggested profile and safe rollback option
Automated rollout gating prevents production regressions (latency and quality monitors) and has runbook documented
Customer adoption pack (playbook + migration checklist + sample SDK patches) published

2026-02-18: Research ran quant-profile comparison on smaller models; found 10-18% cost/speed delta; flagged hallucination edgecases on aggressive int8 for long-context chat

2026-03-10: Field experiment cohort A showed 12% median token cost reduction, latency within SLO; one customer reported minor formatting regressions — triage in progress
risks: Quality regressions with aggressive quantization on long-dialogue customers
Insufficient telemetry granularity for per-route cost attribution in some legacy integrations
Customer pushback if transparent reporting is not clear; risk of churn for large reservation customers
Cross-team bandwidth: several dependent ENG tasks are shared with Dedicated autoscaling work
next_steps: Finalize design for console rollout toggle and rollback flow by 2026-03-20
ENG to prioritize finer-grained request traces (ENG-4017) to enable per-route cost signal by 2026-03-28
Launch expanded A/B with 10 additional customers focused on embeddings workloads by 2026-03-31
